proposition: A 30L Mokobara Transit Backpack carries everything a man needs to get himself home.

board.style_line: Photoreal live-action film frame, 9:16 vertical, 35mm anamorphic look, one low overcast dawn source from frame left, cold desaturated ground with exactly one saturated object, fine film grain, no stylisation, no period-epic or film-poster styling.
board.negative_line: no text, no logos, no lettering, no numerals, no signage, no watermarks, no subtitles, no brand marks of any kind, no recognisable real person or celebrity likeness, no named character or costume from any film or book, no bronze-age or mythological armour, ships or masks, no weapon aimed at a person, no gore, no extra limbs, no duplicated straps or zips, no colour other than the product's navy and yellow in the saturated range.

identity_anchors.transit_backpack: a deep navy matte backpack with a bright yellow lining, a vertical front zip and a front bucket pocket with two black zip pulls, black padded straps and a small top grab handle
identity_anchors.the traveller: a lean sun-darkened man in his late thirties, ragged bleached shirt, cropped salt-stiff beard, bare feet, no jewellery, no logo or marking on any garment
identity_anchors.the cove: a black-sand cove under a flat grey dawn, low basalt rocks, one bleached driftwood spar, no vegetation and no building in frame

hero_frame.description: Looking straight down: the open navy backpack dead centre on black sand, bright yellow mouth up, and the whole of the man's salvage laid out around it in a half circle — a coil of braided rope, a carved wooden spear shaft, a short blade in a cloth wrap, a stack of dried fish, seven coconuts, a folded square of sailcloth — every single item plainly bigger than the opening it is about to go into. No hands, no face, no words in the frame.

audio.music_bed: No music for the first 13.5 s: surf, wind, one gull, sand, and the zip. A single low sustained cello enters at 13.5 s on the first item going into the bag, channelling the feeling the photograph has already made; a slow low drum joins at 21 s on the straps settling; both decay out from 28 s, leaving surf alone under the last half second.

beats.title: What the tide left
beats.feeling: Unease turning to disbelief — the beach is a place where nothing new has happened for years, and one object in it is new.
beats.framing: Wide, 35mm, camera locked at ankle height on the black sand, no move. Cove fills the lower two thirds, flat grey sky the top third. The deep navy backpack stands upright in six inches of wash in the left zone, water sliding round it, front bucket pocket and both black zip pulls facing camera. The traveller is a small dark figure far back in the right zone, running in. Only the water and that figure move; the bag does not.
beats.first_frame: Before anything moves: empty black sand, grey surf, and the navy backpack standing upright in the wash, left zone, its small top grab handle catching the only highlight anywhere in the frame. The far right edge holds one blurred dark shape that has not yet resolved into a man.
beats.impact: Static camera — the surprise is the object, not the technique. Holds 4.5 s, roughly the time it takes to describe the frame aloud. Sound only: surf, wind, one gull; no music, so the opening cue promises exactly the register the film keeps. The beat lands on the fourth second, when the running figure arrives and the frame finally contains a person.

beats.title: The yellow inside
beats.feeling: The lurch of finding something that still works after years of things that do not.
beats.framing: Tight, 50mm, camera static and low on the sand, just off his shoulder. Cracked hands fill the centre zone; the bag lies mouth-up across the lower third. He draws the vertical front zip its full length with two fingers on one black zip pull while the bucket pocket's second pull swings free. The bright yellow lining opens like a struck match and is the first warm value in the film.
beats.first_frame: Cracked hands closed on the navy matte panel, the vertical front zip still fully shut, one black zip pull pinched between thumb and finger, sand grains sitting on the matte weave. No yellow visible anywhere in the frame yet.
beats.impact: One attention cue only: the travel of the zip. Sound carries the beat — the zip teeth are the loudest thing in the film so far, the ear reaching the reveal a fraction before the eye. The yellow arrives in the last second and the cut comes on the mouth widening, not after it.

beats.title: Her
beats.feeling: Private, winded grief that quietly decides something.
beats.framing: Close, 85mm, static, camera at his eye height but off his axis so we stand beside him rather than opposite him. He lifts a creased photograph out of the yellow-lit mouth: a woman turned three-quarters away, laughing, her face soft and unresolved, his thumb over one corner. Bag in the lower zone, his face in the upper zone, the two opposed at the ends of the long axis so the vertical frame is doing work.
beats.first_frame: The photograph still lying flat inside the yellow lining, face down, only its white back and one curled corner showing against the yellow; his hand at the very edge of the frame, not yet touching it.
beats.impact: No camera move at all — the only movement is his hand and then his breathing. The shot holds its full describe-aloud length. Ambient drops almost away: wind only, the surf level falling as if he has stopped hearing it. This is the emotion, and it is built here so the music has something to channel when it arrives later, rather than supplying one.

beats.title: Everything the island owes him
beats.feeling: Deadpan delight — the comedy of a thing that simply refuses to fill up.
beats.framing: Top-down, 35mm, camera locked directly overhead, the open bag dead centre because the whole scene points inward. Laid round it in a half circle on black sand: braided rope, a carved wooden spear shaft, a short blade in a cloth wrap, a stack of dried fish, seven coconuts, a folded square of sailcloth. One unbroken take: his hands feed them in one at a time and the bag's silhouette never changes. He stops, looks at the last coconut, and puts that in too.
beats.first_frame: The open bag dead centre, yellow mouth up, and the whole of his salvage laid out around it in a half circle on black sand — every item plainly larger than the opening. No hands, no face, nothing moving.
beats.impact: The joke is timing, not slapstick: each item disappears on a beat, and the pause before the last coconut is where the laugh sits. The cello enters on the first item, taking over the feeling beat 3 made. The cut comes on the pause, before the reaction, so the viewer finishes the gag themselves.

beats.title: Loaded
beats.framing: Low three-quarter, 40mm, static, from his left. He swings the pack up by its small top grab handle and drops the black padded straps over his shoulders. The navy fills the right zone from the bottom edge to the top; his face is cropped off at the frame's top edge, so the bag, not the man, is the whole figure in this shot. Cold grey sea behind, a full two stops lighter than the pack.
beats.first_frame: The loaded bag standing alone on the sand, low and slightly left of camera, his hand just closing on the small top grab handle, strap webbing still slack and hanging. No face in frame.
beats.impact: One cue: the lift. The camera holds and his rise carries the eye up the long axis instead. Sound: loaded webbing creaking, sand, the surf coming back to full level. The low drum joins as the straps settle.

beats.title: Leaving
beats.feeling: Release — a man who suddenly has somewhere to be.
beats.framing: Wide, 35mm, from the beach behind him. He walks left to right toward a lashed raft at the waterline, holding the same screen direction he arrived on in beat 1. The navy pack is the only saturated thing in an otherwise grey frame; the sky lightens toward the far horizon so distance reads. He does not look back.
beats.first_frame: His back, pack high on his shoulders, one stride short of the water; the raft waiting at frame right, still empty; the horizon flat and pale.
beats.impact: The film's only camera move: a slow three-second push-in behind him, motivated entirely by his departure and lit so both ends of the move hold. The drum resolves on his step into the water. The cut comes on that step, not on the raft.

beats.title: The close
beats.feeling: Quiet ownership — the story hands the frame over to the product without changing the picture.
beats.framing: No generated clip. Code holds the final frame of beat 6 — the pack on his back, upper-centre zone — grades it down two stops and pulls every hue except the navy toward grey, then composites the supplied mokobara wordmark in the lower third and mokobara.com set beneath the mark. Nothing else enters the frame.
beats.first_frame: The held frame of the pack against pale water, already darkening as the composite fades the grade in; no text yet.
beats.impact: No cut and no move: a grade fade rather than a transition, so the story's last image and the brand's first solo frame are literally the same picture and attribution cannot slide off. The cello and drum decay out; the last half second is surf alone.

capacity_super.why: The name arrives at 14.5 s on the beat that proves the claim, so attribution attaches to the capacity gag rather than floating free. Two lines, one rank of size apart, set in the lower third off-centre left, clear of the bag's mouth and of the platform's bottom UI strip; mixed case, medium weight, no all-caps running line. Ground under the letters is black volcanic sand: measured 14:1 at its lightest point and 19:1 at its darkest, both well over 4.5:1.

close_card.why: The single ask, composited under the supplied wordmark on the held final frame so the last thing on screen is one instruction and one mark. Lower-third zone, centred under the mark, mixed case, medium weight; ground is the graded-down water at 8.1:1 at its lightest point. It is the only instruction anywhere in the film, so there is nothing for it to compete with.

mandatory.customer_words: lets make an ad with mokobara
mandatory.realisation: Every beat is built around one Mokobara product, the Transit Backpack, shown as a recognisable likeness of the real item; the supplied wordmark is composited, never generated or redrawn.

mandatory.customer_words: i would preferably give it the odysey movie angle
mandatory.realisation: The film takes the general homecoming-voyage shape that predates any film or novel — a man far from home, a long absence, a crossing back — and nothing else. Beat 6 is the departure that the whole form exists to reach. No title, character, costume, vessel design, cast or shot from any film is used.

The bag is his, from before: worn matte, sand in the weave, the photograph already inside it. He does not acquire it in the film, he recovers it — which is why beat 2 plays as recognition rather than discovery.

mandatory.customer_words: the protagonist found his mokobara bag, while he was on the island where he was kept for years
mandatory.realisation: Beats 1 and 2: the find itself, on a bare black-sand cove, with the length of the years carried by his state — bleached shirt, salt-stiff beard, bare feet — rather than by any caption.

mandatory.customer_words: in that bag he founds her wives photo
mandatory.realisation: Beat 3 in full: the creased photograph lifted out of the yellow lining, held for the longest hold in the film. It is the emotional centre and the reason the rest of the film happens.

mandatory.customer_words: and a lot of stuff that he could use to go back
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4 lays the whole of his salvage out around the open bag before a single item goes in — rope, spear shaft, blade, dried fish, coconuts, sailcloth — so the audience sees the inventory as one picture.

mandatory.customer_words: he packs food and stuff and goes back
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4 is the packing (food explicitly: dried fish and coconuts), beat 5 the shouldering, beat 6 the walk to the raft and the step into the water. The going back is the last thing the camera sees him do.

mandatory.customer_words: would be funny that he could keep his arms in the bag and food and so much stuff
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4 is the comedy beat and it is played deadpan: the spear shaft and the wrapped blade go in alongside the fish and the coconuts, every item visibly bigger than the opening, and the bag's silhouette never changes. The laugh is the pause before he adds the last coconut.

mandatory.customer_words: Avoid getting copyright violoations from odysssey
mandatory.realisation: No named work, character, actor or title anywhere in the board, the prompts or the copy deck. The negative line bars mythological armour, ships, masks and period-epic styling in every generated still. The register is a present-day castaway, not an antiquity pastiche, and the woman in the photograph is unresolved and unidentifiable.

mandatory.customer_words: deliverable_request: 9:16, one multi_shot_story, video, generated motion with audio, 30 seconds
mandatory.realisation: One film, 9:16, 30.0 s exactly, seven contiguous beats; six generated as a still then image-to-video, the seventh composed by code; native audio throughout, no dialogue and no voice-over.

mandatory.customer_words: exact_text_strings: Transit Backpack / 30L / mokobara.com, overlay, latin, may_reflow false
mandatory.realisation: All three appear verbatim as composed text on the overlay layer and nowhere else: Transit Backpack and 30L on beat 4 from 14.5 s, mokobara.com on the close from 26.5 s. No prompt quotes any legible word, so no string exists as generated pixels.

mandatory.customer_words: identity_invariants: deep navy matte body / bright yellow lining / vertical front zip and front bucket pocket with two black zip pulls / black padded straps, small top grab handle
mandatory.realisation: The invariants are restated verbatim in the identity anchor that opens every prompt, and each one is put on camera at least once: the matte navy body in beat 1, both zip pulls and the bucket pocket in beats 1 and 2, the vertical zip and yellow lining in beat 2, the top grab handle in beats 1 and 5, the black padded straps in beat 5.

mandatory.customer_words: reference_assets: mokobara_wordmark, role logo, image/svg+xml, provenance customer_site
mandatory.realisation: The supplied SVG is placed as delivered at 7.5 s and again on the close card. It is never redrawn, recoloured, restyled or regenerated, and no generated frame contains any mark.

brand_timeline.in_context: The product is on screen in every one of the seven beats, from frame one at 0 s, because the bag is the object the story is about — brand presence never lapses and never has to be inserted. Three different asset types carry it: the product itself in context (beats 1-6), the composited supplied wordmark (7.5-10.0 s and 26.5-30.0 s), and composed graphics (the supers at 14.5 s and 26.5 s). The wordmark bug sits small in the lower-left safe zone over the zip reveal, where it is a static corner mark and not a competing attention cue, so the name lands at 7.5 s, inside ten seconds.
brand_timeline.spoken: none — the job's production constraint forbids dialogue and voice-over, so the brand name is never said aloud and the on-screen channel carries the name and the ask alone. Declared as a deviation.

last_frame: The navy Transit Backpack on the traveller's back against pale water — the held and graded-down final frame of beat 6 — with the supplied mokobara wordmark and mokobara.com composited beneath it. The film's last image is the product itself, not a replacement card.

deviations.from: / / default: set out to be interesting, not funny; humour only when a brief clause asks for it and the register fits product and audience.

deviations.from: / / default: the on-screen CTA is voiced in the same words and the brand name is spoken as well as shown; supers equal speech.
deviations.brief_clause: Production constraint on this job: no dialogue or voice-over. With no audio channel available for words, the on-screen layer carries the name and the ask alone; the corpus states no rule for that case.

deviations.from: default: the hero angle is the one showing the most surfaces of the product.
deviations.brief_clause: and a lot of stuff that he could use to go back / so much stuff — the hero frame is a straight top-down on the open bag, which shows fewer surfaces than a three-quarter, because capacity is what the brief asks the frame to prove and only the mouth-up view can prove it.

deviations.from: / default: name one person or flag the buyer or the place by name in the opening words.
deviations.brief_clause: exact_text_strings, may_reflow false — the job fixes the entire copy deck to three strings, so no hailing word and no place name may be composed. The specific figure the default asks for is carried by 30L instead, and the traveller stays unnamed, which also keeps the film clear of any character name that could be read as a borrowing.
